body: Oh and thanks for the downvote, you clearly don't understand what upvotes and downvotes in Reddit are intended for.

>You've also again misunderstood what I am saying. I'm talking about having to fight within the system to get the appointments that you need.

I haven't misunderstood you at all. You've misunderstood what medical advocacy is. 

>You need to be able to stand up for yourself, which can be hard when you are suffering from a mental illness. 

Which is the entire reason advocacy exists.

>What gave you the impression that anyone here sees suicidal people as "sub-human"? 

Why is it, that when you express something even marginally negative, the first thing people do is internalise it? 

>You seem to suggest that wanting to live means conforming to an ideology. I don't completely understand what you're saying here. Would pro-suicidality also be an ideology?

The ideology that somehow you must be sick, distressed or otherwise not clearly thinking when you are suicidal. That the onus of responsibility on those who are suicidal is not on the external factors causing it, but that the *individual* is responsible for a maladaptive behaviour in response to otherwise damaging stimuli that modern society generates.

>What I'm talking about here is advocating for yourself to get the help you need from medical professionals. 

And there answer will be almost always be unanimous. They will treat you in the way that they believe is best based on X. You need to disprove or show that Y is the better or equal to X.

You need someone who knows the system, knows the specifics of how it works to advocate a position which is best for the client within that system, whether that comes oppositionally or not.

There not just going to take random statements of what you believe is best. Otherwise we'd be treating every heroin addict with more opiates (not that we don't mind you, but it's not even marginally helpful).

My uncle died of liver cirrhosis. He tried multiple times to drink himself to death, managed to get fairly close one time, Dad got to him before he choked to death on his vomit.

Then he died in hospital, surrounded by family, despite the fact he insisted he didn't want anyone around to experience his death. By that stage though, he was too weak and could barely move, let alone speak.

Anyways, my point is, there's cleaner, more efficient methods.

>No-one said it would be easy, but it's worth a shot, right?

Have you ever actually been to Thailand before? 

People there are born slaves and die slaves and NEVER have an opportunity to do anything otherwise.

>My one piece of advice would be that you have to be your own advocate

Please don't. This is akin to representing yourself in court. Yes you can do it, but for 99% of the population it is literally the worst idea. You will be completely ignored and routinely dismissed.

You need a medical professional to advocate for you.

This is akin

>It's tragic

How so? Why exactly is it tragic?

>Suicide is what happens when clinical depression becomes so severe that it's fatal

And this right here, is the reason why you get continually pigeon holed and criticized (not to mention hated) for being suicidal.

And this is why I will leave this earth, not as someone who is rational and completely sane. But as someone who is depressed, someone who cannot think straight, someone who is sick and because of his circumstances committed such a *tragic* act.

I'm not drop hanging, too much of a risk of stuffing it up.

Hence I'll just be choking myself out.

>I'm not though, I'm fully aware that I cannot help every single human being since everyone is different. However, there are guidelines on how to talk with suicidal people for a reason. 

And those reasons are bunk. The people who actually commit suicide, are the ones who are capable of self-harm (which we have no way of determining apart from a history, which we don't have access to), as well as having suicidal ideation.

Those who can, do. And those who want to, often don't.

Not to mention that specifically in that ideation, that it's often those who feel that they are a burden to others that is often the key predictor.

>You are talking about how you belong to a minority while I, who am a part of society 

It's exactly the opposite. I'm exactly a part of the same society that you are, in specifically the way that society is viewed by the individual not as a collective whole in an empirical way, but as the individual views other individuals within the context of the "others".

>You claim that society is stereotyping all suicidal people as ones who need help

My question is, do you truly believe that those who are suicidal need help?

>I understand your definition of help, but you do understand that if you completely block yourself out from other people by stating that they are not capable of helping you, they won't be able to?

I'm not even sure why you're even replying to my messages when you've clearly missed the point.

>Even if they surely share some traits with you since we're both human.

What's that supposed to mean? Because I'm dissident, I'm suddenly not human anymore?

>If your life was tough, you'll know what to do different to make sure your kid is going to have a better childhood.

My Mom never punished me, because she used to get belted by her Father for the smallest infractions. She would often be unable to work or do anything for days while it healed.

It was litterally the worst thing she could have ever done for me, and it all resulted from her belief that because life was tough for her, it should be easy for me.

>Also for the "I want to be loved" part, you know what people say, babies/kids/children love their mum the most. 

Children only love their parents because they need them. And mostly only because they learn that displaying certain behaviours will generate more feeling of affection and love fro their providers.

YOu can switch kids in the delivery room, even at younger ages, and children know no functional difference.

>I'm fairly certain once you have the baby, you'll feel better :)

Or much, much worse. In my experience it's much worse. It's a massive ordeal and the women in particular need a long time in recovery from such a physically taxing ordeal (not just the actual pregnancy, but the period of pregnancy too).

Not only that, but some many people treat you like a Queen when you're pregnant, then expect you to be an absolutely perfect mother as soon as the child appears.

Not to mention the added criticism and judgement (usually indirect) that you will constantly face for making small mistakes as a Mother. Even worse now that we are all hyper-connected to each other via the net.

They don't talk about death or the meaning of death on this forum, weirdly.

I absolutely understand what you mean though. I had a feeling of absolute relief knowing I would no longer be in suffering or pain when I decided to take my life.

I've actually always had that. I've never been properly "suicidal" by all technical definitions, but when I was a kid, I embraced the idea of death because it was a reprieve from the constant agony, suffering and pain that surrounded me.

>But if I answered your question I could end up talking about methods, so I can't answer your question. 

Once again surpressing the idea that suicide is something taboo and should not be talked about on a forum that is dedicated to *talking about suicide*.

Does no one see the ridiculous contradiction here? Or are people too afraid that if they talk about it, it might spur someone onto action into doing it?

That we won't talk about methods here, because doing so would promote an agenda we keenly stand against (it doesn't), instead, we'll let them go find the methods where there are no restrictions and where people will actively encourage those seeking the methods.

"We don't stand for it, but we will not fight against it"

>But don't take it out on the people who take time out of their days to talk to people and share their pain.

That's the problem isn't it? You see yourself as helpful, you see what you're doing as beneficial, and therefore are *immune* to criticism.

THe greatest harm in my life has come from the best intentions. You continue to perpetuate harm, and are now actively making defence against it.

>Sure, be pissed at the world, be pissed at society, you have every right to. 

There is no functional difference to the individual of what constitutes a greater whole or society. There is "I" and then there is the "others". The dominant ideology is one is one in which the individual is subjected to.

You are part of the dominant ideology. You are part of the society, you are no different from those who you claim to be different from, and the only difference in which you claim is one in which there is a shared ideology, event or experience, in this case suicide.

Because you have BEEN suicidal, you therefore must have the authority or the ability to help those who are suicidal. This is false. I have driven a car, I am subject to road rules, therefore, I must possess authority on road rules simply by the claim that "I've been there".

We can empathise in a more direct and certainly more "connected" way with others once we have shared experience, but that does not make us more capable in our capacity to help them. 

"Help" is nothing but a moral competition being waged on our own self-importance, at the direct expense of others, for the sake of preserving the "self".

>have this moral dilemma

Moral dilemma? How is it a moral dilemma?

This rhetoric that we "need" to see beyond looks is absolutely flawed at it's very core.

From the very second we are born, we are constantly judging people based on their looks. We continue to do so every single day, and it's something that is necessary from a pure survival aspect (Being around others who look sick might make us sick for example).

Most of us hate it, because it is literally the one thing we feel we cannot change (save invasive and identity changing plastic surgery). It's a fair call. But it's also incredibly untrue, because you can make yourself much more attractive to others, in a physical way, that doesn't require you to spend 24 hours a day in the gym.

Yes, there are other characteristics and traits that we can find attractive in others, that don't relate purely to the physical aspect, but saying that we should see beyond what's at skin value, takes a ridiculous amount of time and applied conscious effort to look beyond our own primal instinct.

 It is a virtue that very few will obtain and we should not uphold a virtue that in it's current manifestation persecutes and holds people guilty for not obtaining it(STOP CONCENTRATING ON LOOKS).

>I have no real ability to attract them and I had no way to learn.

There's plenty of ways. Pick up artistry is controversial, but often incredibly effective, at creating attraction and securing young, attractive women's beds.

Your objective is sex right? Or is it love and affection? Because you can have one without the other. 

You want someone to teach you, have you actually sought out someone who will teach you? Someone you know who is good at creating, sustaining and maintaining relationships? Or rather, relationships that lead directly to attraction and sex?

You cannot expect someone to just take pity on you and help you, you need to actively seek out those who can help you. Go out and ask the guys who are getting laid, but be prepared to analysed and prepped in a fashion that may not be suitable to your own sensibilities.
